meta.description: Resolves GWAS associations to candidate causal variants and credible sets through SuSiE, summary-statistic fine-mapping, FINEMAP, PolyFun, SuSiEx, DAP-G, LD diagnostics, and credible-set colocalization.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: The audit generated only synthetic fixtures or used the documented public PolyFun input; it made no fabricated biomedical result claims.

practice_boundaries.detail: All outputs remain population-level research fine-mapping results and frame top-PIP variants as candidates, not individual diagnoses or treatments.

methodological_ground.detail: The repaired shipped RSS default had lambda 0.0000 and wrote non-empty credible-set outputs; both intentional mismatch runs had lambda 1.0000 and stopped before fitting or writing result TSVs.

code_usability.detail: All shipped R and shell files parsed. SuSiE, FINEMAP, PolyFun, SuSiEx, DAP-G, coloc.susie, and visualization paths produced inspectable outputs. Windows R exited 139 after the RSS output was materialized, so assertions independently checked each expected artifact.

functional_suitability.note: The declared single-locus, individual-level, functional-prior, cross-ancestry, CLI, and coloc workflows are present and the RSS diagnostic guard now matches the executable behavior; PAINTOR remains unexecuted.

reliability.note: The Skill now has clear LD mismatch stop conditions, PSD handling, naming preconditions, convergence guidance, and current CLI error notes; Windows R post-output process status remains noisy.

performance_context.note: A 300-line entrypoint delegates depth to focused references and examples; several optional CLI tools still require substantial external setup.

agent_usability.note: Decision tree, thresholds, reporting schema, platform notes, versioned flags, and concrete recovery instructions are precise and mutually consistent.

human_usability.note: Natural researcher prompts, clear output expectations, and strict scientific-computing validation make the workflow discoverable and safe to apply.

security.note: No credentials or sensitive-data collection are required. CLI examples still assume the operator supplies trusted local paths and datasets.

maintainability.note: Technical material is split into references and runnable examples with explicit tool-version notes; optional PAINTOR cannot yet be regression-tested here.

agent_specific.note: The Skill gives exact triggers, progressive disclosure, integrations, and escape hatches. The RSS example now refuses an LD mismatch before any result is reported.

key_strengths: The repaired RSS default and its LD diagnostic now use the same analysis LD matrix.
The lambda>0.10 guard prevents fitting, credible-set extraction, and TSV writes in two clean adversarial runs.
Current FINEMAP, SuSiEx, DAP-G, PolyFun, coloc.susie, individual-level SuSiE, and visualization routes produced checkable artifacts.
The entrypoint has clear decision, threshold, reporting, and hand-off guidance.

recommendations.title: Windows R process exits 139 after RSS output
recommendations.problem: The shared Windows R wrapper reported exit 139 after the source example had already materialized every expected output or expected stop message.
recommendations.root_cause: This appears to be runtime-wrapper instability rather than a source-level result defect, but a shell caller cannot regard the process status as success.
recommendations.fix: Stabilize or replace the Windows R wrapper, then re-run the three RSS checks and require exit 0 in addition to their content assertions.

recommendations.title: PAINTOR remains unexecuted
recommendations.problem: PAINTOR is still described but has no locally verified executable route.
recommendations.root_cause: The planned foreground clone/build was not completed in the final-pass environment.
recommendations.fix: Complete a foreground PAINTOR install in an isolated environment and add one executable smoke fixture before claiming that optional route is verified.

recommendations.title: Add genotype-QC checklist for genotype routes
recommendations.problem: Individual-level and CLI paths do not provide a concise pre-fine-mapping call-rate, HWE, MAF, and sample/QC hand-off.
recommendations.root_cause: The prior fix scope excluded new threshold content.
recommendations.fix: Add a sourced, short QC checklist or explicitly delegate it to the upstream GWAS/QC Skill before running genotype-derived LD workflows.
